scope: Synthetic RS256 identity protocol validation over real loopback TLS JWKS, actual FastAPI dependency/routes and isolated temporary SQLite

fixture.keys: fresh 2048-bit RSA signing keys and independent TLS key generated for this run; never persisted outside temporary directory
fixture.jwks: Python standard-library ThreadingHTTPServer on random 127.0.0.1 port with fresh temporary certificate trusted explicitly by the real HTTPX AsyncClient
fixture.database: fresh testing=True SQLite database per test, normal Domain and SQLAlchemy execution
fixture.api: actual create_app through HTTPX ASGITransport; only API's outbound client construction is patched to inject temporary CA trust; no HTTP/network response mocks
fixture.cleanup: HTTPX clients closed, DB engine disposed, TLS server shutdown/server_close/thread join, temporary directories removed

coverage: RS256 token -> actual trusted TLS GET /keys -> signature and claims -> DB user lookup -> GET /api/v3/me returns reader despite JWT role=admin
JWT role=admin cannot authorize POST /api/v3/users: 403 from actual admin route
old key valid initially; old/new overlap both accepted; old key rejected immediately after removal; new key still accepted
unknown kid, two distinct RSA signing keys with identical kid and wrong signature: generic 401
HS256 and none algorithm tokens: generic 401
expired exp, future nbf, wrong issuer/audience/tenant; null/list/integer tenant; null/integer/list/object sub: generic 401
same valid signed token accepted before DB deactivation and denied with 403 after deactivation; unregistered subject: 404
actual TLS server returns malformed JSON or HTTP 503: generic 401
actual TLS server returns 302 to valid same-origin target: generic 401 and target never requested
actual TLS JWKS delays beyond actual five-second HTTPX read timeout: generic 401, elapsed at least 4.5 seconds

results.warning: Existing Starlette TestClient emits HTTPX deprecation warning; no failure.

limitations: No real enterprise identity provider, enterprise tenant/user mapping or organization policies have been supplied or validated.
This is direct JWT/JWKS resource-server validation, not browser login, OIDC discovery, authorization-code/PKCE, logout or IdP revocation integration.
TLS uses a local test certificate and explicit trust injection; deployment trust store/proxy/network behavior is not validated.
SQLite is used only with testing=True; production PostgreSQL identity execution is not claimed by this report.
API requests execute in-process ASGI; outbound JWKS requests use actual TLS sockets. HTTP serving/proxy deployment is outside this report.
Only scoped authentication/API regressions were run here; this report does not claim a full backend suite run.
